160,935 km2. The page gives no area; it describes the Lower Volga valley and delta, most of Astrakhan Oblast and the right-bank steppe of Kalmykia, with the Caspian to the south and the Nogai Horde to the east. The gazetteer's Astrakhan Oblast plus Kalmykia is about 112,000 km2; the shape adds about 50,000 km2 (to 50 E on the Caspian shore) that the page does not describe, so treat its edges as soft. Cliopatria's 160,935 km2 (1468-74), 161,772 km2 (1475-1501) and 162,622 km2 (1502-55) shapes are one outline within 1 percent; the changes between them are not events.
161,772 km2, the same outline as 1468. Contarini visited the khanate in 1476 and the page describes no territorial change in 1475.

162,622 km2 for 1502-55; the same outline. The page gives no territorial change at 1502 (the Great Horde fell and Ahmed's descendants took the Astrakhan throne, see the 1502 rename). The Crimean occupations of 1523 and 1549 were brief and left the shape unchanged. The khanate ends in 1556, one year after the shape.

region.text: the Lower Volga valley and Volga Delta around Astrakhan (Xacitarxan)

ledger.note: 1466: Mahmud bin Küchük's Astrakhan Khanate breaks away from the Golden Horde. 'The khanate is said to have been founded in 1466' (the page calls the date uncertain and notes Mahmud wrote to the sultan claiming the area as his patrimony in 1466); the Great Horde page has Mahmud, usurped by his brother Ahmed in 1465, 'headed to Astrakhan, seceding'. Cliopatria's first shape is 1468.

1502: Ahmed's line takes the Astrakhan throne as the Great Horde falls. The Great Horde page: the rivalry ended 'with Ahmed's descendants occupying the throne of Astrakhan in 1502'; the Astrakhan page: it 'did not become fully separate from the Golden Horde until the Horde ended in 1502'. The state and its land continue (dynasty change, rule 2).

region.text: Astrakhan and the khanate on the Lower Volga and Volga Delta

ledger.note: 1523: Crimea occupies Astrakhan. 'It was twice briefly occupied by Crimea' (here 1523, under Mehmed I Giray); the Nogai page adds that the Crimean army and khan were destroyed by the Nogais near Astrakhan.

region.text: Astrakhan and the khanate on the Lower Volga and Volga Delta

ledger.note: 1523: the Crimean occupation ends within the year. Nogai Horde page: '1523 Crimea briefly takes Astrakhan, but its army and Khan are destroyed by the Nogais'; Mehmed I Giray was killed near Astrakhan.

region.text: Astrakhan and the khanate on the Lower Volga and Volga Delta

ledger.note: 1549: Crimea occupies Astrakhan again under Sahib I Giray; the page says only that it was 'twice briefly occupied by Crimea' and gives no month.

region.text: Astrakhan and the khanate on the Lower Volga and Volga Delta

ledger.note: 1549: the second Crimean occupation was brief; the page gives no end date, so the end is entered in the same year as a bridging judgment.

region.text: Astrakhan and the khanate on the Lower Volga and Volga Delta

ledger.note: 1554: Russia takes Astrakhan town and installs a client khan. 'In 1554 he fled the town and Russia imposed its client' (Dervish Ali Astrakhani, who soon intrigued with the Crimeans); in 1551 Yamghurchi had made a 'nominal submission to Moscow', then allied with Crimea and the Nogais, and Russia 'sent 30,000 troops against him'. Nogai page: 'helped to take Astrakhan' (Ismail Khan, 1554). Drawn as contested; the Tsardom's dossier may draw the client as a vassal.

region.text: Astrakhan and the khanate on the Lower Volga and Volga Delta

ledger.note: 1556: the contest ends in Russian occupation. 'Russia sent more troops and occupied Astrakhan in 1556, proceeding to destroy the largest slave market on the Volga.'

region.text: the whole khanate: 'conquered and annexed the Astrakhan Khanate'

ledger.note: June 1556: Russia annexes the khanate. Don Cossacks page: on 2 June a Cossack regiment under Ataman Lyapun Filimonov, with Muscovite strelets, 'conquered and annexed the Astrakhan Khanate'; the Astrakhan page has 'Dissolved: 1556, with the Russian conquest'.

region.text: the khanate's land passes to Russia

ledger.note: 1556: the Astrakhan Khanate ends. Month from the Don Cossacks page (2 June); the Astrakhan page dates the dissolution to 1556 only. Astrakhan town was moved 12 km south in 1558. The Crimean Khanate page: 'After the collapse of the Astrakhan Khanate in 1556' the Nogais moved their allegiance to Crimea.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Astrakhan

zones.text: Astrakhan town and the khanate on the Lower Volga

wars.outcome: Russian victory: a client khan installed in 1554, Astrakhan occupied in 1556 and the khanate annexed; the Nogais lost their tribute.
wars.note: Yamghurchi's 1551 nominal submission and revolt brought 30,000 Russian troops; Ismail Khan's Nogais 'helped to take Astrakhan' in 1554 (Nogai Horde page), while the Crimeans were the Astrakhan khan's allies.

wars.name: Crimean occupations of Astrakhan

zones.text: Astrakhan, twice briefly occupied by Crimea

wars.outcome: Two brief Crimean occupations, 1523 (under Mehmed I Giray, whose army was destroyed by the Nogais near Astrakhan) and 1549 (under Sahib I Giray); no lasting change of border.
wars.note: Nogai Horde page for the 1523 destruction of the Crimean army.

certainty.note: Steppe and river-delta frontiers with the Nogai Horde, the Great Horde and Kazan are approximate; the page describes the land only in words.

sources.title: Astrakhan Khanate
sources.note: Identity, 1466 founding, territory in words, the 1523/1549 Crimean occupations, 1551-56 Russian conquest. The page gives no area, no vassalage and nothing after 1569.

sources.title: Great Horde
sources.note: Mahmud bin Küchük secedes after the 1465 usurpation; Ahmed's descendants on the Astrakhan throne in 1502.

sources.title: Don Cossacks
sources.note: 2 June 1556 conquest of Astrakhan by Don Cossacks and strelets; the Don Host territory that the Cliopatria 1642-1768 shape actually depicts.

sources.title: Crimean Khanate
sources.note: Opened for the 1523 and 1549 occupations and Crimean claims: silent on both and on Hajji Tarkhan; confirms the 1556 collapse and that Crimea claimed succession to the Golden Horde, meaning rule over Kazan and Astrakhan (no year).

sources.title: Nogai Horde
sources.note: Nogai help in 1554, 1523 Crimean defeat near Astrakhan, 1556 annexation ended Nogai tribute.

notes: Cliopatria's Astrakhan Khanate row has a second, unrelated life 1642-1768 (five shapes, 124,767-126,354 km2, centroid 42 E 49.3 N, Russia and Ukraine). Its outline is the same as the Don Cossacks row's last shapes (1640-41, 126,353.9 km2, same bbox), so the row is the Don Host carried on under the wrong Name; the khanate itself ended in 1556 and Cliopatria has no Astrakhan shape for 1556-1641. All five are marked wrong; the don-cossacks dossier should extend the Don Host over 1642-1768 (and beyond: the Don Cossacks page says the Host lasted to 1918). The page gives no area for the khanate; the shape (about 155,000 km2 on the gazetteer grid) is larger than Astrakhan Oblast plus Kalmykia (about 112,000 km2). The page's infobox lists the Golden Horde and the Nogai Horde as predecessors and the Tsardom of Russia, Kalmyk Khanate and Nogai Horde as successors; only the Russian handover is dated. The Seshat page (ru_astrakhan_khanate) was not opened; the page budget (5) was spent on five Wikipedia pages. The Crimean Khanate page is silent on the 1523 and 1549 occupations (they rest on the Astrakhan page, the first also on the Nogai page) and says only that Crimea claimed succession to the Golden Horde, 'asserting rule over the Kazan and Astrakhan Khanates', with no year. The 1569 Ottoman-Crimean failure at Astrakhan falls after the khanate's end and is not entered. The Russian client of 1554-56 is drawn here as contest; eu-16 may prefer vassal. No ruler list is entered (the infobox gives only Makhmud 1466 and Darwish Ghali 1554-56).
